narrative.intro: Clark Construction Group is an active federal contractor with $495M in contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The company won 17 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $29.1M, and obligations are up 0.6% year over year. The Department of Defense is the dominant buyer, providing $415M of obligations, followed by the General Services Administration with $76.9M. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest market for Clark Construction Group, accounting for $316M, while Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and Site Preparation Contractors account for $145M and $33.7M respectively. Clark Construction Group’s fiscal-year obligation history shows earlier peaks and troughs: FY24 reached $1.6B, FY23 was $603M, FY25 was $492M, and FY21 and FY22 were $167M and $178M. Current-year totals are partial and reflect fiscal year to date activity. This summary focuses on contract obligations, and it distinguishes total contract value when award tables list award-value figures rather than obligations.

sections.heading: Which agencies are the biggest customers for Clark Construction Group?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the biggest customer, providing $415M in obligations in FY2026 to date. The General Services Administration follows with $76.9M. Smaller buyers include the Smithsonian Institution at $1.6M, the Department of Justice at $1.2M, the Department of Health and Human Services at $953K, and the Department of Homeland Security at $10K.

sections.heading: What federal markets and contract types does Clark Construction Group work in?
sections.body: Commercial and Institutional Building Construction is the largest market with $316M in obligations in FY2026 to date. Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction accounts for $145M, and Site Preparation Contractors accounts for $33.7M. The fiscal-year obligations show work across larger construction programs and civil engineering contracts, with prior fiscal peaks at $1.6B in FY24 and $603M in FY23.
